name: Maldacena-Qi Eternal Traversable Wormhole
description: A wormhole in two spacetime dimensions that stays open for ever. It is anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity, with its two boundaries coupled to each other: the coupling makes negative energy in the quantum fields between them, which holds the dilaton static, and light crosses from one boundary to the other. Two coupled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models share its gravitational dynamics.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

history: Anti-de Sitter space in two dimensions is a strip, $ds^2 = L^2(-dt^2 + d\sigma^2)/\sin^2\sigma$ with $0 < \sigma < \pi$, whose two edges are two boundaries [maldacena2018]. A light ray leaving one boundary reaches the other after the global time $\pi$, so the strip "behaves like a traversable wormhole", in the words of Juan Maldacena and Xiao-Liang Qi [maldacena2018]. Its boundary conditions alone are not consistent in a quantum theory of gravity with excitations of finite energy, as Maldacena, Jeremy Michelson, and Andrew Strominger found in the throat of an extreme black hole, where "all finite-energy excitations of $AdS_2 \times S^2$ are suppressed" [maldacena2018, maldacena1999].¶Nearly anti-de Sitter boundary conditions are consistent, and Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity describes them: a dilaton $\phi$ holds the curvature at $R = -2/L^2$, and on the physical boundary it takes a large fixed value $\phi_r/\epsilon$ [maldacena2018]. Ahmed Almheiri and Joseph Polchinski built models of this kind to study backreaction, and in them the time on the boundary becomes a dynamical variable [almheiri2015, engelsoy2016]. Kristan Jensen rewrote a generic theory of gravity near such a throat as "a novel hydrodynamics coupled to the correlation functions of a conformal quantum mechanics", whose dual is maximally chaotic [jensen2016]. Maldacena, Douglas Stanford, and Zhenbin Yang, and Julius Engelsöy, Thomas G. Mertens, and Herman Verlinde, each wrote the gravitational dynamics as a single time on the boundary with the Schwarzian derivative for its action [maldacena2016, engelsoy2016]. In the words of Maldacena, Stanford, and Yang a year later, "the whole dynamics reduces to the motion of the boundary in a rigid $AdS_2$ space" [maldacena2017].¶A static dilaton that grows toward both boundaries needs negative energy: one equation of the metric, the Raychaudhuri equation of two dimensions, integrates along a light ray from boundary to boundary to $-2\phi_r = \int dX^+\,T_{X^+X^+}$, with $X^+$ the affine parameter along the ray [maldacena2018]. So the null energy along the ray has to be negative, and matter obeying the integrated null energy condition cannot supply it, a special case of the topological censorship that forbids traversable wormholes in asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter spaces of more than two dimensions [maldacena2018, galloway1999]. Ping Gao, Daniel Louis Jafferis, and Aron C. Wall coupled the two boundaries of the eternal BTZ black hole by a double trace deformation, $\delta S = \int dt\,d^{d-1}x\,h(t,x)\mathcal{O}_R(t,x)\mathcal{O}_L(-t,x)$, switched on after a time $t_0$ [gao2017]. The quantum stress tensor then carries "negative average null energy, whose gravitational backreaction renders the Einstein-Rosen bridge traversable" [gao2017]. Maldacena, Stanford, and Yang followed the effect into nearly anti-de Sitter space, where the coupling pulls the two boundaries toward each other and brings them into causal contact [maldacena2017].¶Maldacena and Qi left the coupling on for ever, $g\sum_{i=1}^N\int du\,O^i_L(u)O^i_R(u)$ between $N$ operators of dimension $\Delta$ at equal times on the two boundaries [maldacena2018]. With $N$ large the two boundary times $t_l(u)$ and $t_r(u)$ obey one action, a Schwarzian for each boundary and a term from the coupling [maldacena2018]. The vanishing of its $SL(2)$ charges picks the solution $t_l = t_r = t'\tilde u$, with $(t')^{2(1 - \Delta)} = \eta\Delta$, for the rescaled time $\tilde u = Nu/\phi_r$ and $\eta$ the coupling in the same units [maldacena2018]. Both boundaries then sit at constant $\sigma$, the dilaton does not depend on $t$, and the strip is "a traversable wormhole that is static and time independent, an eternal traversable wormhole" [maldacena2018]. For free fermions the coupling becomes a boundary condition that passes part of each wave from one edge to the other, and their energy on the strip gives the dilaton $\phi = \phi_h\left(1 + (\pi/2 - \sigma)\cot\sigma\right)$, up to a constant [maldacena2018]. Its excitations fall into the towers $t'(\tilde\Delta + n)$ of $SL(2)$, with the gap $t'\Delta$, and the gravity adds one oscillator of frequency $t'\sqrt{2(1 - \Delta)}$, the boundary graviton [maldacena2018].¶The same action governs two copies of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model, $N$ Majorana fermions with random couplings among $q$ at a time, joined by $H_{\rm int} = i\mu\sum_j\psi^j_L\psi^j_R$ [maldacena2018, sachdev1993]. At low energy each copy has the Schwarzian action Maldacena and Stanford derived, and the coupling adds the term the gravity has, so the two systems share one gravitational sector [maldacena2016remarks, maldacena2018]. Their ground state is close to the thermofield double of the two uncoupled models at a temperature set by $\mu$, and at large $q$ equal to it [maldacena2018]. Heated, the coupled models pass from thermal anti-de Sitter space at low temperature to two black holes at high temperature in a Hawking-Page transition, and in the microcanonical ensemble the two phases are continuously connected [maldacena2018]. Cooled from a pair of black holes by a colder system, they settle into the wormhole, which Maldacena and Qi offer as a practical way to prepare two copies of the model in the thermofield double state [maldacena2018].¶Two nearly extreme black holes held close together could supply the coupling, with fields whose fluctuations near the two are correlated, as Maldacena and Qi suggested [maldacena2018]. Maldacena, Alexey Milekhin, and Fedor Popov built it in four dimensions, from a pair of extreme black holes of opposite magnetic charge in Einstein and Maxwell's theory with charged massless fermions [maldacena2023]. The lowest Landau level gives each fermion as many massless fields in two dimensions as there are quanta of magnetic flux, moving along the field lines, and their negative Casimir-like energy holds the throat open [maldacena2023]. The throat is anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a sphere in global coordinates, with a symmetry under the global time of the strip and no horizon [maldacena2023]. It is fragile, and enough energy sent into a mouth makes a pair of horizons [maldacena2023].

coordinates.name: Global

parameters.description: The radius of curvature, a length; the Ricci scalar is $-2/L^2$ everywhere
The least value of the dilaton, dimensionless, at the middle of the wormhole; it sets the negative energy of the matter fields

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \sigma)$, both dimensionless, and the dilaton is $\phi = \phi_h\left(1 + (\pi/2 - \sigma)\cot\sigma\right)$, with $T_{tt} = T_{\sigma\sigma} = -\phi_h$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: The radius of curvature, a length; the Ricci scalar is $-2/L^2$ everywhere
The least value of the dilaton, dimensionless, at the middle of the wormhole; it sets the negative energy of the matter fields

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t_P, z)$, both dimensionless, and the dilaton is $\phi = \phi_h(1 + x\arctan x)$ with $x = (1 + t_P^2 - z^2)/2z$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

parameters.description: The radius of curvature, a length; the Ricci scalar is $-2/L^2$ everywhere

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t_R, \rho)$, both dimensionless, and the dilaton is $\phi = \phi_h(1 + x\arctan x)$ with $x = \sinh\rho\cosh t_R$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
